transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Next: Establish WHERE the water appears, WHEN in the cycle, and what it LOOKS like before choosing a part. Let me know what you find.

ok I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, should I get out of it first?? the fuse box is in the hall and the floor there is dry, so I can switch it off from there. the water is mostly at the front under the door

Yes, step out of the water now and don't touch the machine, the plug or the socket while the floor is wet. Because the water has reached the plug, turn the power off at the fuse box in the hall, where you'll be standing on a dry floor, before you go near the machine again. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

ok I'm out of the water now and going to switch it off at the fuse box. It started today in the middle of a wash, and the display was still counting down with normal washing sounds and no burning smell. I think there was a small damp patch last week but I thought I'd just spilt a drink.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Is the leaking water clean, soapy/dirty wash water, or dirty/oily-looking water?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
it looks like clear soapy wash water I think, not oily or dirty. the power's off now at the fuse box. what should I check next?

Next: If it started after cleaning the filter, re-seat the filter cap/seal and check the sealing face before suspecting the pump. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I haven't touched the filter at all, so I don't think that's it. Do you mean I should go and look at the machine now? The power's off but the floor by the plug is still wet, I'm not sure it's safe to go near it.

Yes, as long as the power is switched off at the fuse box, it's safe to go and look at the machine. Don't touch the plug, socket or switch while that floor is wet, and keep the power off until everything around the plug is completely dry. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the pump filter cap or its seal. The pump filter cap at the bottom front is a common leak, especially if it's been opened recently. Check it's screwed in fully and straight, and that its rubber seal is clean. Was it loose or not seated, tight and dry already, or is the cap or seal cracked or damaged?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

ok, the filter cap flap area is dry and the cap is tight. But I looked at the door rubber and there's a small split in the bottom fold, with an underwire from a bra stuck right next to it. Is that the problem?

Yes, that split is very likely the cause. A tear in the bottom fold of the door seal lets soapy wash water escape during the wash, which matches the clear water you found mostly at the front under the door, and the underwire stuck beside it has probably worn or cut the hole. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal (boot). Next: If the door seal is ripped, check the drum for up/down play, a dropped drum or bearing noise so a replacement seal isn't destroyed too. Let me know what you find.

I'm not sure how to check that, sorry. The machine is full of water and heavy and I can't move it on my own. The washing sounds were normal earlier, if that helps. Is the split seal definitely what needs sorting?

Not definitely, but it's the most likely culprit: clear soapy water pooling at the front under the door, with a split in the bottom fold of the seal and the pump filter cap tight and dry, fits a door seal leak well. An engineer will need to confirm it and check whether anything else, such as the underwire, has caused damage elsewhere. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal.
